applicability.rationale: The active validateLifecycleV3ContentsScoped path fully validates each history transaction and then repeats current validation when an exact V1 revoked current value equals the final tail in the same call.

confidence.rationale: Exact v2 artifacts, v1 correction chain, current source, charge/memo behavior, optional-state validation, deep-copy fixture construction, every new mutation, downstream strong gates and immutable-base applicability were inspected directly.

impact.rationale: The patch changes the shared strict lifecycle V3 validator used for persisted recovery records and internal candidate sealing. A mistaken shortcut could admit malformed recovery authority, history, execution or reconciliation state.

importantCallers: recovery begin and revoke publication paths

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Current merely shares an ID or PlanSHA with history, differs in a nested transaction field, or equals a non-tail entry.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Current validation may be reused only when the same complete transaction was already validated as the final history item in the same call under identical root time and revision.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The history loop validates before recording the ID, and the shortcut requires reflect.DeepEqual against the final history value; post-reuse duplicate/final-tail equality remains enforced.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: V1 with Source, COMPLETED, FAILED_RECONCILED, Execution-bearing, Reconciliation-bearing or V2 missing-checkpoint state reaches reuse.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Only V1 REVOKED_UNSTARTED with nil Source, Execution and Reconciliation may reuse validation; every other shape must fail earlier or take the complete current path.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Explicit shortcut conjuncts exclude each shape; corrected current-only fixtures preserve a valid history and force current fallback, while the V2 missing-checkpoint fixture intentionally proves the complete-history early gate.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: current Recovery arm and history planContext

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Plan reseal fails before root validation, or mutating current also mutates the history tail and makes DeepEqual vacuously true.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Each negative must reach its documented validator boundary after root reseal without helper fatal or mutation aliasing the comparison side.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Each subtest begins with lifecycleV3Copy, which canonical-encodes and decodes a fresh graph; current-only Plan values are copied before mutation, pointer fields are separately decoded, nonTail is not mutated after assignment, every case uses lifecycleV3Seal, and illegal V1/V2 Source combinations deliberately avoid plan reseal.

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Current equals the first valid history transaction instead of the final tail, or changes only an allowed Revocation reason while keeping Plan and PlanSHA unchanged.
materialBoundaries.invariant: A previously seen ID and an unchanged PlanSHA must not substitute for full final-tail transaction identity.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The non-tail fixture assigns the complete valid first history transaction, then relies on the unchanged final-tail gate; AUTHORITY_CHANGED is an allowed revocation reason, so the same-plan fixture remains generically valid and is rejected by complete DeepEqual rather than plan digest.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: generic current validation followed by duplicate-ID/final-tail gate

materialBoundaries.counterexample: The duplicate current call is the only place that charges work, creates checkpoint state, initializes a target memo or consumes authority.
materialBoundaries.invariant: Reuse must not skip a required work charge, decode-scope effect, memo initialization or authority-producing side effect.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: The existing root charge includes history plus current; V1 planContext only checks Source and returns the already constructed context; final-tail descriptor validation already handled the exact target; nil Execution returns immediately; validation does not grant authority or mutate the record.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: lifecycle V3 decode scope, V1 plan validation context and nil execution validator

materialBoundaries.counterexample: Root/hash/canonical/owner gates are bypassed, timeouts or test counts are relaxed, or a candidate-only runtime is treated as causal speedup.
materialBoundaries.invariant: The source shortcut must not weaken record integrity/custody controls or be described as a measured performance improvement.
materialBoundaries.legitimateControl: Only two Go files change; 688 tops, 256 entries, 2 MiB and 180 seconds remain fixed; measurement instructions require immutable same-flags source AB/BA before benefit claims.
materialBoundaries.runtimeRoot: strict decode, candidate seal, store publication and future Linux measurement

protectiveFactors: Every history transaction is validated before its unique recovery ID enters recoveryIDs.
Reuse requires the seen ID, nonempty history, exact V1 schema, nil Source, REVOKED_UNSTARTED, nil Execution, nil Reconciliation and full reflect.DeepEqual equality with the final history item.

The function-level decode charge still includes the current item; V1 planContext has no decode-scope mutation; the exact target memo was populated or checked by history validation; nil Execution validation would return without side effects.
The duplicate-ID/final-tail gate and all owner, fence, trusted-time, retired-epoch, root, canonical, size, custody, sealing and publish/readback controls remain unchanged.
The v2 test table corrects the v1 setup-fatal later-schema case and adds focused current-only, non-tail and same-plan-digest cases without a new top or product hook.

recoverability.rationale: The two-file change is revertible and introduces no migration or wire-format change. Because the validator protects persisted lifecycle and authority state, a latent false acceptance would require record/evidence review in addition to reverting.

regressionLikelihood.rationale: The shortcut is narrowly source-supported and the corrected same-top fixture matrix now covers each required fail-closed partition without an evident setup fatal or alias leak. Likelihood is not low because neither changed Go file has been formatted, compiled or executed.

regressionProtection.rationale: The existing test top now contains a generic-current positive, exact-tail positive and twelve resealed negative subcases, including corrected current-only, non-tail, same-plan-digest and history-early-reject partitions. Static reachability is supported, but no Go, gofmt, Linux or 688-name execution ran.

riskDrivers: The optimization is an unconditional shared-validator branch with no rollout switch.
No Go syntax/type check, gofmt, Linux 688-top run, full-suite completion or fresh checker evidence exists.
No exact-source same-flags AB/BA measurement exists; performance benefit and timeout causality remain unproven.

statusQuoRisk.rationale: The duplicate validation is source-proven, but its performance contribution is not measured. The capacity test previously passed while a different full-suite test was unfinished at timeout, so no correctness or causal performance benefit is established.

unknowns.summary: Whether v2 formats, compiles, executes every corrected subcase, passes all 688 required Linux tops and full/fresh checkers remains unknown.
Whether the shortcut produces a reproducible same-flags AB/BA performance improvement or closes the 180-second full-suite timeout remains unknown.
